scenarios.name: a fresh dropdown on the page: Did Mount in the first frame, Value 'Option 1' (the first default option), Enabled true, the three states false, Child Index 0, This itself
a pick: the keyboard goes onto the element (Focused), Value 'Option 2' is sent and Changed fires; the same option picked again: nothing — it is already selected; the first again: Value and Changed

Value from the graph: Value sent, no Changed; the same again: nothing; null: ignored; the number 5: '5' (matching no option, the selection stays where it was); undefined: kept and not sent — a pick of the first option then sends it with Changed

a pick, then Value written to the picked value: nothing (the node already holds it); Items written after it: nothing — the pick stays; Value written to the other option: Value sent, no Changed, and the selection follows — picking that option raises nothing, picking Option 2 again sends it with Changed

a pick, then Value written back to what the author set before the pick: Value sent, no Changed, and the selection follows on the interpreter — on the runtime the component's effect keys on the author's Value React last rendered, which this write did not change, so the pick stays selected and picking it again raises nothing

Items written with the current Value absent: nothing on the wire, and the new list hands the selection to its first option — a pick of it raises only Focused; a pick of 'l': Value 'l', Changed; Items written again: the pick stays, nothing on the wire, and the new list, which lacks it, hands the selection to its first enabled option — a pick of it raises nothing, a pick of 'c' fires Changed

a pick, then Mounted off and on: Will Unmount; Did Mount, and the dropdown is where the person left it — nothing on the wire; a pick of the same option raises only Focused (the element that came back did not hold the keyboard)
a disabled option cannot be picked: nothing; its enabled neighbours can; a value the list does not offer: nothing
Items null: no options, a pick finds nothing; an empty list: the same; a list again: the selection comes back; Items written undefined: no opinion, the list and the selection stay
Items written undefined over a list of its own: no opinion — the list stays, so a pick of 'l' sends it with Changed

the selected option leaves the list: the browser hands the selection to the first enabled option of the new list while the node keeps its value — picking that first option raises nothing, picking another fires Changed
placed with a Value no option has: the fresh element selects its hidden empty option, the span shows the placeholder; a pick of the first option sends it with Changed

an option without a Value is picked by its Label's text; items that are not options offer the empty value, which a pick of '' meets as already selected — with the graph confirming each pick (Value written to it the frame after; v3: without it the runtime's effect takes the author's Value back at a remount or a new list, row D34)
with a label: a pick still works, the keyboard goes onto the `<select>` inside the wrapper

a pick, then Enable Label turned on: the <select> and the keyboard stay — the next picks select with no Focused; a Blur action gives the keyboard up (Blurred); turned off again, a pick takes it back (Focused) — the runtime rebuilds the <select> and the keyboard leaves with the old one, silently (was row C80, fixed in P109 ISL-031)
Placeholder and every look or layout input change nothing on the wire
a Label that is an object with Enable Label on: the label is drawn as its text and the page keeps drawing

placed on 'Option 2' with a third option: a pick of the first and a Value write to the third in one frame — Value once (the write's) and Changed once; a Value write back to the second and a pick of the third in one frame — Value ends where it began and is not sent, Changed once

a person acts on a painted page: Mounted written off and an act in the same frame find no element (a Focus after it is Unchanged); written on, the act meets the element (a Focus after it is Done) — every act, both ways — with the graph confirming each pick (Value written to it the frame after; v3: without it the runtime's effect takes the author's Value back at a remount or a new list, row D34)

a person acts on a painted page: Enabled written off and an act in the same frame meet a disabled element (a Focus after it takes nothing, a Blur gives nothing up); written on, an enabled one — every act, both ways

a person acts on a painted page: Enabled and Mounted both written and an act in the same frame — off together (no element; a Focus after it Unchanged), on together (Did Mount, an enabled element) — every act, both ways — with the graph confirming each pick (Value written to it the frame after; v3: without it the runtime's effect takes the author's Value back at a remount or a new list, row D34)

a person acts on a painted page: Enabled off with Mounted on (a disabled element arrives: Did Mount, the act takes nothing, a Focus after it Done and nothing focused), then Enabled on with Mounted off (the element leaves) — every act, both ways

the matrix: every act, enabled or disabled, with the keyboard off or on the element, remounting in the act's frame or not, after a pick or not, with Items rewritten in the frame or not — then a Focus action in the same frame; every segment starts from a fresh element with the label off — with the graph confirming each pick (Value written to it the frame after; v3: without it the runtime's effect takes the author's Value back at a remount or a new list, row D34)
a disabled dropdown takes no click, press, release, focus or pick — the pointer still hovers it, and a finger reports nothing (C64)
the Focus action puts the keyboard on the `<select>` (Focused, Done); again: Done alone; Blur: Blurred, Done; again: Done alone
Enabled off and a Focus in the same frame: the dropdown is still enabled on the page, so it takes the keyboard; in the next frame a Focus is Done and takes nothing
focused, then disabled: Focused stays true — a disabled element gives the keyboard up to nobody, so a Blur is Done and nothing fires; re-enabled, Blur takes it
Mounted off after a pick: Will Unmount; Value keeps the pick; a click and a pick find nothing; a Focus is Unchanged; Mounted on: Did Mount and nothing else — the dropdown is where the person left it
Enabled follows its input as a boolean and is sent only on a change
placed disabled: a Focus before the first frame is Done and takes nothing — the element was drawn disabled
a press held, then disabled and re-enabled across frames, then a click: Pressed true until the click's own release ends it

focused, then Mounted off and on: the leaving takes the keyboard and Focused with it — Will Unmount, Focused false and Blurred (D30); Did Mount; a Focus action puts the keyboard on the element that came back and fires Focused; a Tab away then fires Blurred
Enable Label turned off while the pointer is over the dropdown: the label goes, the dropdown stays where it is, and a leave afterwards still ends the hover

Enable Label turned off, then the Focus action: the dropdown is on the page and takes the keyboard (Focused, Done) — on the runtime the label-off rebuild nulled the root ref (two elements, one ref; was row C66, fixed in P109 ISL-031), so Focus reports Unchanged
disabled and unmounted in one frame, then enabled and remounted in one frame, then a quiet frame: Did Mount once, Enabled true, and nothing more
placed disabled, Mounted off then on with a press in the same frame: Did Mount and nothing else (a disabled element takes no press); a Focus after it Done and nothing focused; the same with a release

focused, then Enable Label turned on and a press in the same frame: the dropdown keeps the keyboard — the press fires Pointer Down with Pressed and no Focused; turned off again, a Tab onto it finds the keyboard there already — the runtime rebuilds the <select> and the keyboard leaves with the old one, silently (was row C80, fixed in P109 ISL-031)
Mounted off then on, and a Tab onto the dropdown in the same frame: Did Mount and Focused together; the same with Enabled off: Did Mount alone, a Focus after it Done
a press held across a frame, then the release and a Blur action in the same frame: Pointer Up, then Blurred — the keyboard the press gave is still there to take away
focused, then the pointer onto the dropdown and a Blur action in the same frame: Hover Start, then Blurred — a hover alone moves no keyboard

a pick, Mounted off; Mounted on and a Tab onto it in the same frame: Did Mount and Focused — the pick stays and the fresh element took the keyboard; a Tab away and a pick of the same option: Blurred, Focused and nothing more; the same with Enabled off: Did Mount alone

a pick and a Tab away, then Items written and a Tab onto the element in the same frame: Focused alone — the pick stays; a Tab away and a pick of the same option: Blurred, Focused and nothing more; the same on a disabled element: nothing
Mounted off; Mounted on and a pick of the option the fresh element already selects in the same frame: Did Mount and Focused, no Changed; disabled: Did Mount alone

focused, then disabled: a press, a release, a click, a Tab onto it, a Tab away and two picks meet a disabled element and move nothing — the keyboard is still on it, so re-enabled, a Blur action fires Blurred

a pick, a Tab onto it, then disabled; in one frame Items rewritten with an act — the act moves nothing on a disabled element; Items rewritten keeps the pick; re-enabled, a Blur action fires Blurred — every act, each segment from a fresh element — with the graph confirming each pick (Value written to it the frame after; v3: without it the runtime's effect takes the author's Value back at a remount or a new list, row D34)
Visible off: a hidden dropdown is under no pointer and takes no keyboard — every act raises nothing; the Focus action is Done with nothing; shown again, a click is a click
Visible off in the frame of an act: the act's paint hides the dropdown first — the act raises nothing; one that held the keyboard keeps it (no focus fixup), and a blur takes it off

a hidden dropdown brought back with Mounted in the frame of an act: the act's paint puts it on the page (Did Mount) and the act reaches nothing — a Focus action after it is Done and takes nothing; every act
Visible off after the keyboard is on the dropdown: it keeps it (no focus fixup), so a choose still lands; blurred, a choose reaches nothing
hidden and holding the keyboard: a hover meets nothing and takes nothing away — a choose still lands
hidden, holding the keyboard: every pointer act meets nothing and takes nothing away — the Blur action after each finds the keyboard on the dropdown (Blurred)

a pick, the keyboard taken off, then Items rewritten and a mouse press in one frame: the pick stays and the press puts the keyboard on the dropdown (Pointer Down, Pressed, Focused) — a Blur action next frame gives it up (Blurred)
Items written as the old stored text: its options are offered, and choosing 'b' moves Value to 'b' with Changed
Items written a number: no options are offered and the page keeps drawing; a list written after it is offered, and choosing its second option 'y' moves Value with Changed
Items written an empty list, then a list of one: the browser selects 'x' as it arrives, since nothing was selected, so choosing 'x' is no change — no Value, no Changed
a fresh dropdown offered nothing keeps its hidden option selected when a list arrives, so choosing the list's first option 'x' moves Value with Changed
a list holding an empty item: the item is skipped and the others are offered — 'a' is selected by the browser's reset, and choosing 'b' moves Value with Changed
a Placeholder that is an object, with nothing selected: drawn as its text, and the page keeps drawing — choosing 'Option 2' moves Value with Changed
a param's write is a sample: placed with Value 0 and handed Value undefined before the first settle, the first frame sends Value '0' (only the initial state is not a sample)
a plain store reads nothing: zIndex written, then Value undefined, before the first settle — the first frame sends no Value (the 'Option 1' the node held is never read by the store)

hidden, holding the keyboard, Enable Label changed with every pointer act: the act meets nothing and the keyboard stays — the Blur action after each finds it on the dropdown (Blurred); shown again, the dropdown takes the keyboard (the Radio Button's scenario)

focused and under the pointer, then Mounted off, an act and a Focus action in one frame: the act's paint takes the element off the page, and Focused and Hover with it — Will Unmount, Blurred and Hover End (D30) — so the act finds nothing and the Focus is Unchanged; Mounted on: Did Mount; every act

the keyboard on the dropdown with no pointer over it (a Tab put it there), then Mounted off and a Tab away in the same frame: the blur's paint takes the element — Will Unmount and Blurred at the act — so a Blur action after it blurs nothing (Done, no second Blurred) and a Focus action focuses nothing (Unchanged); Mounted on: Did Mount

Mounted written off in the frame of an act while the element holds the keyboard, a finger, or both (a press) — every act: the act finds the element leaving, so its states go with it (Blurred for the keyboard; Will Unmount), and a Focus after it is Unchanged; then back on, a fresh element holding nothing
